changes: The protocol core is stateless and no longer depends on an initialize session exchange.
Multi Round-Trip Requests replace server-initiated interactions that required a continuously held stream.
Method and tool headers enable gateway routing and policy enforcement without parsing request bodies.
List responses carry cache hints and deterministic ordering.
Tasks are an extension; authorization adds issuer validation and moves away from Dynamic Client Registration toward Client ID Metadata Documents.
Roots, Sampling, Logging, and legacy HTTP plus SSE are deprecated with a stated migration window.
production_implications: Do not require sticky sessions merely to host a conformant remote MCP server.
Keep application task state explicit even though the transport core is stateless.
Validate authorization issuers, bind credentials to issuers, and plan migration away from deprecated registration patterns.
Version clients, servers, extensions, and tool contracts independently; protocol adoption does not remove tool-level authorization or idempotency work.
watch_items: Extension interoperability and enterprise authorization adoption
SDK migration behavior across supported languages
Removal dates and replacement maturity for deprecated features

change_log.summary: Adopted the stateless core, extensions framework, Tasks lifecycle, authorization hardening, cache hints, and formal deprecations as the project baseline.

changes: Version 1.0 is the first stable protocol release.
The release adds multiple protocol bindings, version negotiation, multi-tenancy support, and signed Agent Cards.
Task results can be consumed through polling, streaming, or webhooks.
A2A remains complementary to MCP: it addresses independent-agent interoperability rather than agent-to-tool access.
production_implications: Use A2A when an agent boundary is also a product, platform, vendor, or organizational boundary; use an in-process contract for local decomposition.
Verify agent identity and metadata, negotiate versions, scope tenant identity, and persist task state independently of a live stream.
Treat webhook delivery, replay, authorization, and artifact retention as application responsibilities.
watch_items: Operational guidance for signed Agent Cards and trust roots

change_log.summary: Moved the project baseline from pre-1.0 drafts to the first stable release and recorded the enterprise migration implications.

changes: GenAI semantic conventions moved out of the core semantic-conventions documentation into a dedicated OpenTelemetry repository.
The dedicated model covers GenAI client signals, agents, MCP, provider conventions, spans, metrics, and events.
The repository still identifies schema-version work as incomplete, so adopters should not imply a single frozen production schema.
production_implications: Pin the semantic-convention revision used by instrumentation and record it with telemetry pipeline versions.
Translate provider-specific traces into a controlled internal contract instead of coupling every consumer to a moving upstream field set.
Collect prompts, retrieval queries, tool arguments, and outputs only under explicit privacy, retention, and access policies.
watch_items: Published schema URL and versioning policy
Stability levels for agent and MCP signals

change_log.summary: Updated the baseline to the dedicated OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-conventions repository and marked it as evolving rather than stable.

changes: The project now has an agent-specific risk baseline rather than relying only on LLM application risks.

The taxonomy covers goal hijack, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse, supply chain, unexpected code execution, memory poisoning, inter-agent communication, cascading failures, human-agent trust, and rogue agents.
production_implications: Threat-model goals, tools, identities, memory, inter-agent boundaries, and cascading side effects as separate attack surfaces.
Connect design controls to adversarial tests, runtime detection, incident response, and recovery; a policy paragraph alone is not an enforced invariant.
Use the Top 10 as a coverage checklist, not proof that a system is secure or compliant.
watch_items: Revisions to the threat and mitigation taxonomy
Crosswalks to other governance and security standards
New incident patterns that change control priorities

change_log.summary: Established the 2026 Agentic Top 10 as the fieldbook's current agent-security coverage baseline.
